We need propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a tolyl (para methyl phenyl) attached to sulfonamide linking to another phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually structure: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline (with an extra NH on aniline? Actually Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with an extra amino group? That's a phenyl with two amine substituents? The SMILES: ...Nc3ccccc3N means amide attached to an aniline where the aniline has an NH2 at para? Actually c3ccccc3N is an aniline (aniline). The preceding N is the amide nitrogen attached to that aniline carbon (C=O)N-Ph-NH2? Wait: C(=O)N c3ccccc3N: carbonyl attached to N which is attached to phenyl that also has an NH2 substituent (maybe at para). So final product has three aromatic rings, a sulfonamide, an α,β-unsaturated amide.

We need 3 reactions: likely (1) sulfonamide formation (attach sulfonyl chloride to aniline). (2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid then amidation? Actually forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. In retrosynthesis, we can break the C=C and carboxylic acid to aldehyde + malonic acid. Then amide formation from acid to amide.

Thus steps: target -> disconnect amide bond to give carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then disconnect the C=C to give aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Then disconnect sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1) and aniline (the first phenyl with methyl). Actually sulfonamide formed between sulfonyl chloride and aniline (the p-tolyl-sulfonyl part attached to the second phenyl). Wait sulfonamide is between NS(=O)(=O) linking the two phenyl rings: the nitrogen attached to the first phenyl (p-tolyl) and sulfonyl attached to second phenyl. So retrosynthesis: break N-S bond to give sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph) and aniline (p-tolyl-NH2). So three steps: (1) amide formation, (2) Doebner modification, (3) sulfonamide formation.

We need template IDs for each step. Need to search for templates matching these transformations.

First, amide formation: functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, functional_groups_formed: amide. Use search.
